title: Cheezechoice

title: Code 365
description: A full-stack learning and interview-prep platform with 360+ DSA problems, SQL practice, interactive visualizers, and company-specific preparation.
imageCaption: A structured learning experience helps developers build skills and prepare for technical interviews.
body: Code 365 is a learning and interview-preparation platform for developers who want a more organized way to build practical skills. It brings data structures and algorithms, SQL, and technical interview resources into one place, so learners can move from studying a concept to practicing it without jumping between tools.

The problem library includes more than 360 data structures and algorithms questions, alongside a dedicated collection of SQL exercises. Daily challenges, flashcards, and structured study plans give learners several ways to keep a steady routine, revisit important ideas, and decide what to work on next.

Practice is built around an interactive editor powered by Monaco. Developers can work through problems directly in the platform, while visualizers and learning tools for algorithms, Git, and SQL help make abstract topics easier to understand. The goal was to support both deliberate study and hands-on experimentation in the same workflow.

Code 365 also connects practice to interview preparation. Mock interviews, company-specific questions, and interview experiences help learners focus their preparation around the roles and organizations they care about. Streaks, statistics, achievements, and rankings make progress visible and provide useful milestones along the way.

I built the application with Next.js 14, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Radix UI. Supabase handles authentication and PostgreSQL data storage, while Gemini supports AI features. The platform is deployed on Vercel, bringing the learning experience together as a full-stack product.

content.text: A guided path from learning to practice

Code 365 brings data structures and algorithms, SQL, and interview preparation into one learning environment. Its library of more than 360 DSA problems and dedicated SQL exercises gives developers a place to practice, while daily challenges, flashcards, and study plans help turn that practice into a steady routine.

content.alt: Code 365 learning dashboard with study shortcuts and progress statistics
content.caption: The dashboard puts a learner’s next steps and progress in one place.

content.text: The platform pairs hands-on problem solving with tools that make concepts easier to explore. A Monaco-powered editor supports coding practice, and algorithm, Git, and SQL visualizers give learners an interactive way to work through ideas. Learning paths organize related topics into a sequence, helping users understand what to study next.

content.alt: Code 365 learning path showing an Arrays and Strings module and its lessons
content.caption: Structured modules break broad topics into focused lessons and practice.

content.text: Code 365 connects regular practice to interview goals with mock interviews, company-specific questions, and interview experiences. Streaks, statistics, achievements, and rankings help learners review their momentum and see how their work adds up over time.

I built the application with Next.js 14, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Radix UI. Supabase handles authentication and PostgreSQL data storage, while Gemini supports AI features. The platform is deployed on Vercel.

title: Chatura Solutions
description: A career upskilling platform offering expert-led courses, mock interviews, and guidance to help learners move forward.
imageCaption: The landing page brings course discovery, consultation booking, and career guidance together.
body: Chatura Solutions helps learners build skills and move toward their career goals through expert-led learning, mock interviews, and career guidance. I shaped the website around that promise, giving visitors clear ways to explore courses or book a consultation.

The site brings its learning offer and support together in one place, with course discovery, consultation booking, and resources easy to find. I built it with WordPress, Elementor, and the MS-LMS plugin, using Calendly to support consultation scheduling.

title: Smart Mart
description: My first full-stack project: an ecommerce platform with product discovery, cart and wishlist, order management, authentication, and payment integration.
imageCaption: The cart brings selected products and order totals together before checkout.
body: Smart Mart was my first full-stack project, built as a learning project rather than freelance work. I used it to understand how an ecommerce product works across the entire stack, from browsing a product catalog and managing a cart to placing an order and reviewing its status. It includes product search and category filtering, a wishlist, checkout, order history, and invoice generation.

Building the frontend and backend together gave me practical experience connecting user actions to application data. Angular and Angular Material power the storefront, while Spring Boot and Hibernate provide the backend services. The application uses a relational database, JWT-based authentication, and payment gateway integration, with admin screens for managing products and orders.

content.text: Smart Mart was my first full-stack project, and a chance to build an ecommerce experience end to end. I brought product discovery, a wishlist, cart management, checkout, and order history into one application, following the shopper from the first browse through a completed order.

content.alt: Smart Mart product catalog with category filters and product cards
content.caption: The product catalog lets shoppers browse and filter available items.

content.text: I used Angular and Angular Material for the storefront, then connected it to backend services built with Spring Boot and Hibernate. This helped me learn how a screen action—such as changing a cart quantity or submitting an order—needs to travel through the application and be reflected in persistent data. The project supports MySQL or PostgreSQL and uses JWT-based authentication for customer workflows.

content.alt: Smart Mart cart with item quantity controls, order summary, shipping address, and checkout button
content.caption: The cart summarizes items and costs before the shopper checks out.

content.text: After checkout, customers can review their orders and see delivery status. On the admin side, order management provides a view of customer, product, quantity, and status details, with controls to update fulfillment progress. The project also explores payment integration and invoice generation.

content.alt: Smart Mart order history showing an order, its details, and delivery status
content.caption: Order history gives customers a view of their purchases and delivery progress.

content.alt: Smart Mart admin orders table with customer, product, amount, quantity, and status columns
content.caption: The admin order view supports reviewing orders and updating their status.

content.text: On the operational side, Log4j supports application logging and audit trails. Together, these pieces make Smart Mart more than a static storefront: it connects shopping, payment, support, and monitoring in one application.

title: Drona LMS
description: A production-ready, microservice-ready LMS foundation with a Spring Boot backend, PostgreSQL, JWT authentication, and a separately planned AI service.
imageCaption: A modular service foundation for learning management and future AI capabilities.
body: Drona LMS is a production-ready, microservice-ready foundation for a learning management system. The current backend uses Java 17 and Spring Boot, with PostgreSQL persistence and JWT-based authentication secured by Spring Security.

I organized the workspace around separate services: the Spring Boot backend, an Angular frontend, and a FastAPI AI service. The frontend and AI service are planned components, with architecture, database, and endpoint documentation guiding their integration.
The stack is designed to run together with Docker Compose. The project currently uses NeonDB for hosted database storage, with a migration to AWS planned.
